sections.title: Getting started
sections.summary: New here? The Set up guide walks you through it (macOS is automatic; Windows needs a one-time loopMIDI setup). After that: connect the controller and start Live. The script starts the Maschine Bridge, which takes over the hardware: no Controller Editor, no MIDI mode, a real SHIFT key. While Live loads, the screen shows Waiting for Live; when the set is ready, a rainbow wave sweeps across the pads. Your note repeat rate, arp settings, chord type and voicing, drum colours and velocity curve are remembered between Live sessions.

notes.title: Using the MASCHINE plug-in (Expansions)
notes.text: NI's MASCHINE plug-in (VST / AU) takes the controller as soon as it is anywhere in the set, and keeps it until it is deleted: selecting another track or switching the plug-in off doesn't release it. Meanwhile the script steps aside: the lights, screen and pads are MASCHINE's, and Live's status bar says so. Delete the last MASCHINE plug-in and the controller is back with Live within about a second, on the drum pads or the keyboard. To switch between the two on the fly, use v1.6.1 (in the same download) in NI's MIDI mode, where SHIFT + MASCHINE (MK3, MASCHINE+: SHIFT + CHANNEL) switches between MASCHINE and Live. Or play the Expansions' kits without the plug-in: STAR > MASCHINE Kits (see STAR: browse and load).

items.does: The real SHIFT button: hold it for the second function printed on a button, and for the SHIFT + pad edit matrix.

sections.title: Highlights
sections.summary: The best of it in a minute. Each one is explained in its own section below.

items.does: A real controller, not a template: a real SHIFT key and Live's colours on the pads. No Controller Editor, no MIDI mode.
The screen shows almost anything: the mode and track, tempo, swing and volume as you change them, and device parameters with their names and values.
A chord on every pad, always in Live's key: triads to 9ths, with voicings.

Note repeat that follows pad pressure: slide the touch strip to set its rate, or touch it while holding pads to repeat them on the spot. Plus an arpeggiator and 16 velocities, all recorded exactly on Live's grid.
A step sequencer on the pads, read like MASCHINE, with the playhead running across them.
Live's browser on the hardware screen: find a sound and load it without touching the mouse.

MASCHINE Kits: play your Expansions in Live without the MASCHINE plug-in. STAR > MASCHINE Kits, turn to hear a kit, push to load it as a Drum Rack, pad for pad as in MASCHINE; SHIFT + STAR marks a favourite.
Record a variation in one press: the clip is copied below, named Bass_1, Bass_2 ..., and recorded into; the original stays untouched.
The touch strip shows where the loop is, and while you record it flashes red on every click: a silent metronome.

sections.title: PATTERN: clips
sections.summary: A 4x4 view of Live's Session clips (4 tracks x 4 scenes). Pad colours follow the clip colours; playing clips are bright. Recording a new clip (an empty slot, or VARIATION + pad) selects its track, so Live's auto-arm arms it (the dimmed arm, which follows the track you select; tracks armed for real are disarmed), and the pads switch to the drum pads or the keyboard so you can play into it right away.

items.does: Tap: switch to clip mode. Hold + PAD: launch a clip, then return to the previous mode.

Launch the clip. On an empty slot of a MIDI track: select that track (Live's auto-arm arms it) and record a new clip there; the pads switch to the drum pads or the keyboard so you can play right away.
Duplicate that clip into the next slot.
Delete that clip.
Move the clip view left / right by one track.
Move the clip view up / down by one scene.
Move the clip view by four tracks.
New: stop recording and select the next empty slot (ready to record).

The strip lights show how far the selected track's playing clip is through its loop, in the clip's colour; while it records, the bar flashes red on every metronome click (a silent metronome). Touch the strip to jump within the loop (on Live's launch quantization).

sections.title: SCENE: scenes
sections.summary: 16 scenes on the pads, in their colours, in the order of Live's scene list: scene 1 top left (pad 13), then to the right and down. Playing scenes are bright, triggered scenes flash.

items.does: Tap: switch to scene mode. Hold + PAD: launch a scene and return.
Launch the scene. An unlit pad creates a new scene.
Duplicate the scene.
Delete the scene (the last scene can't be deleted).
Scroll the scenes by one (SHIFT: by 16).
Capture and insert scene (copies what is playing into a new scene).
The strip lights show the playing clip's progress in the scene's colour. Touch the strip to jump all playing clips within their loops.

sections.title: TRACK: tracks on the pads
sections.summary: Your tracks read like text: track 1 on pad 13 (marked A), track 2 on pad 14 (B), then to the right and down. The return tracks and the Master always sit on the last pads (two returns: pads 2 and 3, Master on pad 4); TURN scrolls the other tracks. Colours follow the tracks; muted tracks are white.

items.does: Tap: show tracks on the pads (latched). Hold + PAD: act on a track and return.
Tap: show tracks on the pads (latched). Hold + PAD: act on a track and return.
Select the track. A group track folds / unfolds.
Create a new MIDI track.
Create a new audio track.
Arm that track and disarm the others, like Live's mixer (again: disarm). SHIFT + SELECT + PAD adds a track, to record several at once.
Solo / unsolo that track (works from any mode: the pads show tracks while SOLO is held).
Mute / unmute that track (from any mode).
Stop that track's clips (from any mode).
Duplicate the track.
Delete the track (not the Master, not the last track).

sections.title: PAD MODE: drums
sections.summary: The 16 visible pads of the track's Drum Rack. Hitting a pad plays it and focuses it in Live (like MASCHINE focusing a sound). Pads are coloured by chain colour or by name (see the colour table). While a clip plays, the pads of the notes it plays light up.
sections.swatches_note: Name colours: pads use their chain colour by default; press PAD MODE again to colour them by name instead (it is remembered). A chain without a colour also gets its name colour. The name is read word by word, first word first, as sample names start with the kind of sound (Kick BlackEarth 1, ClosedHH Dev, BD_Deep_01); a word counts when it starts with one of these words, and short abbreviations (BD, SN, HH, OH ...) only as whole words. Anything else is white.

items.does: Switch to drum mode. Press again: switch between chain colours and name colours.
Play and select the drum pad. Velocity and pressure (aftertouch) are sent.
Select the drum pad without playing it.
Mute / unmute the drum pad.
Solo / unsolo the drum pad.
Erase that pad's notes in the focused clip (no clip: empty the pad).
Copy the first pad onto the second.
Scroll by one row (SHIFT or PUSH + TURN: by 16 pads).
Previous / next drum pad: focuses that sound (named on the screen; the one STEP sequences).
Velocity curve: Linear / Soft / Hard.

sections.title: KEYBOARD: notes in key
sections.summary: The pads walk up Live's current scale (root note bright). Root and scale are Live's own, so changing them here changes Live's Scale settings and vice versa, including per-clip scales. While a clip plays, the pads of the notes it plays light up.

items.does: Switch to keyboard mode.
Play the note.
Choose the setting TURN changes: Octave, Root or Scale. The screen shows the setting and its value.
Change the chosen setting (Octave to start with).
Change the scale (Live's scale list).
Change the root note.
In key / chromatic layout (Live's Scale Mode).
Erase that note's events in the focused clip.

sections.title: CHORDS: chord sets
sections.summary: Every pad plays a chord built from Live's scale, starting on successive scale degrees, so every chord is in key. A chord you play, or one the clip plays back, lights its own pad bright and the pads of its other notes softer (the C chord: the E and G pads), so you see its shape.

items.does: Switch to chord mode. Press again: next chord type (Triad, 7th, 9th, Sus2, Sus4, 6th, Power).
Next voicing (Close, Inversion 1, Inversion 2, Spread).
Play the chord (works with note repeat and the arpeggiator).
Choose the setting TURN changes: Octave, Root, Scale, Chord or Voicing. The screen shows the chord and key, and the chosen setting with its value.
Change the chosen setting (Octave to start with); SHIFT + TURN: scale; PUSH + TURN: root note.

sections.title: STEP: step sequencer
sections.summary: The pads are 16 steps of the focused sound (the focused drum pad, or the last keyboard note) in the focused clip, read like text as in MASCHINE: step 1 top left (pad 13), step 16 bottom right (pad 4). The playhead runs across the pads while the clip plays, and the page follows it on longer clips (after you change the page yourself, it follows again once the playhead reaches your page).

items.does: Switch to step mode.
Add / remove a note on that step. On an empty slot, the first step creates a one-bar clip.
Next / previous page of 16 steps (◀ ▶ too).

Choose the sound to sequence: while SELECT is held the pads show the sounds (the drum pads, or the keyboard), brighter where the clip has notes and brightest for the current one. Press one to pick it (you hear it); let go and the pads are its steps. The screen names the sound.
Next / previous sound: the next drum pad (named on the screen), or the next note of the scale.

sections.title: Playing: velocity, repeat, arp, touch strip
sections.summary: The bridge plays the notes itself, next to the hardware, so the pads can do things one-note-per-pad MIDI can't: chords, arpeggios, note repeat that follows pressure, 16 velocities.

items.does: Fixed velocity on / off: every pad plays at the same velocity (100 unless you change it).
Set the fixed velocity (1-127): holding FIXED VEL shows it on the screen at once. Remembered next time.
16 Velocities: all pads play the focused note, pad 1 softest to pad 16 hardest.

Hold: note repeat while held. Tap: latch on / off. From clip or scene mode it brings up the drum pads or keyboard until repeat stops. With note repeat or the arpeggiator, the pads flash with their notes (a latched arp keeps them flashing). Repeats and arp notes follow Live's beat and land exactly on its grid when you record (Live's Record Quantization is set to the rate while they run, then put back); each note lasts the whole step (100 % gate), like MASCHINE.
Turn the NOTE REPEAT button into the Arpeggiator (the screen says which); again: back to Note Repeat. Holding or tapping NOTE REPEAT then works the same way for both.
While NOTE REPEAT is held, the screen shows its setting and value until you let go. Note Repeat: the rate (1/2 to 1/64, triplets too). Arpeggiator: the setting chosen with ◀ ▶. Turn to change it.

Arpeggiator: choose the setting TURN changes: Rate; Type (Up, Down, Up/Down, Down/Up, As Played, Random, Chord); Octaves (1-4); Gate (note length; 100 % fills the step); Latch (On: the arp keeps playing your last notes after you let go of the pads, and new pads replace them).

The arpeggiator, step by step: 1. SHIFT + NOTE REPEAT once (the screen says Arpeggiator). 2. Hold NOTE REPEAT and hold a chord on the pads: it arpeggiates. 3. Still holding NOTE REPEAT, use ◀ ▶ to pick Rate, Type, Octaves, Gate or Latch, and TURN to change it; the screen shows it. 4. Tap NOTE REPEAT instead of holding it to keep the arp on hands-free; tap again to stop.

Note repeat rate; touching the strip starts note repeat while you touch it, also for pads you are already holding (hold a pad, then touch the strip), and shows the rate. Otherwise the strip lights show the selected track's playing clip, like in PATTERN mode, flashing red on every metronome click while it records (a silent metronome). A new recording fills the strip over 4 bars; after that every new bar starts at 3/4 and fills to the end, like on MASCHINE. In PATTERN, SCENE and PLUG-IN mode touching the strip has its own job (see there).
Touch strip becomes a pitch bend (springs back when released). Press again: back to rate.

sections.title: EVENTS: select notes
sections.summary: Hold EVENTS: the pads show the drum pads or keyboard of the mode underneath; lit pads have notes in the focused clip.

Press one (or the clip): the clip is copied there, its track selected (auto-armed), and the copy focused and recorded into, while the original stays as it was. While Live plays, the copy launches and recording overdubs it once it plays; when Live is stopped, Live counts in first (Session Record), then plays and overdubs the copy. A full column gets a new scene. From PATTERN, SCENE or TRACK the pads switch to the drum pads or the keyboard to play; in the play modes and STEP you stay where you are. The copy is named after the original with the next number (Bass → Bass_1, a variation of Bass_1 → Bass_2; an unnamed clip → 1, 2 ...).

sections.title: Tempo, swing, volume
sections.summary: Hold the button: the screen shows the value at once; turn the encoder to change it, and let go to go back. A quick tap shows the value for a moment.

sections.title: PLUG-IN: device parameters (MIKRO)
sections.summary: The encoder controls one parameter of the selected device at a time. Parameters come in pages: Ableton's own banks for Live's devices (Filter, Envelope...), the visible macros of a rack, or groups of 8 for plug-ins. The screen shows the device, the page and how many there are (Macros 2/2; on two lines, the device and the count at the right of the track name when they fit), and the parameter's name and value. A rack shows as many macros as it shows in Live: click the rack's + macro button for up to 16. Each device remembers where you were.

items.does: Parameter mode on / off.

Previous / next page (a rack: Macros 1-8, 9-16). The screen shows the page and the count, e.g. 2/2.

Tap: reset the parameter to its default.

The strip lights show the parameter's value as a bar, in the track or rack chain colour; a rack's macros each have their own colour (macro 1 orange ... macro 16 red, like MASCHINE's sounds). Touch the strip to set the value. PITCH / MOD take the strip over while they are lit.

sections.title: STAR: browse and load (MIKRO)
sections.summary: Live's browser on the hardware screen, in the order of Live's sidebar: Collections first (Favorites and your coloured collections), then MASCHINE Kits, the library (Sounds, Drums, Instruments ...), and the folders you added to Places. MASCHINE Kits (Live 12.1 or later, with MASCHINE Expansions or the MASCHINE library installed) lists your Expansions and their kits: PUSH on a kit loads it as a Drum Rack, pad for pad as in MASCHINE: onto the selected MIDI track, replacing its instrument (effects after it stay), or on a new MIDI track named after the kit (# Kit name, so Live numbers it) when an audio track is selected. Each pad is a Simpler in 1-Shot, so a hit rings out; long synth, vocal, FX, atmosphere and loop sounds play while held instead. The pads and the Drum Rack's chains get the drum colours by sound name (see PAD MODE). A drum-synth sound plays NI's recording of it where there is one; a sound that is a plug-in in MASCHINE (Massive, Monark ...) stays an empty pad with its name, to put your own sound on. Turning onto a kit plays NI's own preview of it through Live's preview (Cue output, preview switched on in Live's browser), like clicking a sample in Live's browser; the script puts the previews in your User Library (MASCHINE Kit Previews, as hard links: no extra disk space) the first time you open MASCHINE Kits, and picks up newly installed Expansions the same way. This is the way to play the Expansions in Live without the MASCHINE plug-in, which takes the controller away from the script (see Getting started).

sections.summary: Your preferences, on the controller. They are saved with Live's preferences on your computer, remembered after a restart, and take effect at once.
